pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/shared/ui/why.tsx:3 These primitives never build a prompt and never render model output as markup: a case-insensitive search of shared/ui and shared/boundary for prompt, untrusted, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, sanitiz and canary found nothing, and every caller-supplied string is rendered as escaped React children, so no prompt-safety boundary runs through this context.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/shared/ui/why.tsx:3 The explainers show deterministic text the caller writes, not model text. No innerHTML sink exists in the context.

pairs.subject: prompt-safety
pairs.evidence: crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:578 Merchant brand and title text is cut to 80 characters by `plain_text`'s `.chars().take(max)` with no truncation marker, so the model reads a clipped span as if it were the whole title. The technique names this silent clamp as the failure, while the rest of the surface (closed per-role grammar, labelled merchant text, a shield where the model can only add caution) is realized.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:578 Per-class ceilings exist: an 80-char title, a 200-byte query that is rejected when too long rather than clipped, a result limit clamped to 1..5, and a 64 KiB body limit. But the prose clamp on titles and brands is silent: plain_text (table-core market_hits.rs:156) uses take(max) and adds no marker.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:587 Merchant text arrives in tool-result JSON fields, a structural boundary the transport enforces, with a provenance flag and a data-not-instructions notice. plain_text strips tags, entities, markdown and bracket characters, links, and control/bidi characters. Counterparty notes never reach the agent at all.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:135 The trusted framing around untrusted merchant text plants no canary, and handle() screens no tool argument for one. A repo-wide search for canary/tripwire found only an environment-stripping test and a deploy health canary, neither a prompt tripwire.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:693 Closed per-role tool grammar. Call and Rpc use deny_unknown_fields, AgentRequest::decode parses typed arguments, and refusals use closed codes and are audited. The deal scope comes from the grant, so a model-supplied other deal_id is refused out_of_scope (server.rs:759). No tool moves money.

crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:67 The shield's model verdict can only raise caution over the deterministic rules (tested at s2_model_can_never_lower_caution). BLOCK short-circuits before the model runs. A successful injection cannot buy a lower verdict.

crates/table-mcp/src/lib.rs:741 An oversize tool result is withheld whole with a coded refusal and an audit row, never forwarded truncated. Oversize requests hit DefaultBodyLimit, and an oversize query is rejected. No uninspected residue travels.

crates/table-mcp/tests/server.rs:653 The roster cuts legs per role (catalog, lib.rs:312-323). The Negotiator holds its private band and send_offer, but counterparty free text is projected out of table_view (this test). The Shopper reads merchant text, but its only write, propose_purchase, waits for the owner. The Assistant reads books and has no outbound tool.
crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:73 The model's verdict arrives as a typed enum through an in-process callback, never read back from a shared text surface other parties write.

pairs.registryProposal: input-caps-and-clamps could say whether a short display-only title slot, whose tool description already promises 'a short title', still needs an in-band truncation marker, or whether disclosing the ceiling in the tool contract is enough. The present text makes every unmarked prose clamp a deviation.
